text: Airborne fungal diseases covered: (1) Damping-off (Fusarium, Rhizoctonia, Pythium, Phytophthora) — kills young seedlings at the base within ~2 weeks of transplanting, caused by weak/wounded seedlings and contaminated nursery soil/media; prevention is nursery hygiene and clean media; treatment chemicals referenced include Metalaxyl, Fosetyl-Al, Dimethomorph, Copper Sulfate, Carbendazim. (2) Downy mildew (Pseudoperonospora cubensis) — favored by high humidity/rain and 25-30°C, yellow-to-brown angular leaf spots; prevention is resistant varieties, avoiding overhead evening watering, adequate plant spacing for airflow; treatment chemicals: Metalaxyl, Fosetyl-Al, Chlorothalonil, Azoxystrobin+Propineb, Mancozeb. (3) Anthracnose (Colletotrichum orbiculare) — circular brown leaf lesions with yellow halos, mainly on older leaves near the base; treatment chemicals: Mancozeb, Chlorothalonil, Pyraclostrobin, Azoxystrobin, Difenoconazole. (4) Powdery mildew (Podosphaera xanthii) — white powdery fungal growth on leaf/stem surfaces; treatment chemicals: Azoxystrobin, Myclobutanil, Thiophanate-methyl, Chlorothalonil. (5) Gummy stem blight (Didymella bryoniae) — brown stem lesions oozing amber gum; treatment chemicals: Pyraclostrobin, Chlorothalonil, Azoxystrobin, Copper hydroxide. General prevention across all five: field sanitation, crop rotation away from recently-infected cucurbit fields, and avoiding evening overhead irrigation.
